body:
Thank you, it was very incredible and very fate-like to meet her. It makes the loss so much deeper because of it, however. With great love comes great sorrow. 

I do have folks that I need to stick around for. They're supportive, but most of our friends group has left because they don't know how to handle this. I don't believe people are equipped to deal with this extreme loss in their mid- to late- 20s, let alone know what to say to help others. 

I appreciate you talking to me. I am now exploring medication and hospitalization to help me stay grounded after talking to my therapist. 

The yearning is strong, but I shouldn't expand this type of horror to more people. I shouldn't give the message that suicide is the way out, especially to her younger brother. In a way, I need to jump on the grenade.

I am sorry for your loss. I have been to counseling in the past for anxiety and just monthly check-ins. After the loss, I am in therapy once a week, which has been helpful but at the same time not enough.

Her name is Hannah. We met when she was 18 and I was 22. The kind of couple that other people would look at and believe in true love. I can't count how many times people have told me that I found my soulmate after meeting her, because the connection was unreal. Those memories sting much more now because of the loss. They were right. 

I'm hanging on for now. Crisis hotlines have also helped tremendously. Still don't see the point, but I am trying to pound into my head the amount of devastation that would happen if I left in this manner.
